name: Customer API failures
ownerWords: do we have api portal staging? your job is PM for api portal
goal: Real customers' calls on api.virev.ai do not fail for causes on our side. The 5xx answers of the last full UTC day stay at most 1% of every keyed customer call in prod ClickHouse product.customer_usage_events (crawl_read and data_api_request rows, house orgs and org_test_ proof orgs left out), the rows the API portal alert, board 52 and billing read. This keeps board goal p80 met: about 31% of customer calls failed from 10-13 to 10-26, and p80's fixes (crawler 403 and 404 verdicts, the portal passing a 403, a 404 and an Instagram 429 through, the empty-account user_feed page in 9b2c02d7f) brought the day to 0.67% on 10-31 and 0.32% on 11-01. source_errors holds the read itself, because until 11-26 the duty read PostHog and its query hit PostHog's max execution time on every run from 11-21. slow_route_over_target_s keeps board goal p111 met (owner 10-30: "이거 왜 20초 30초나 걸리냐"): the most seconds any slow route's p90 gateway duration of the day, by every org and internal ones included, sits over that route's own target in the precheck's ROUTE_P90_TARGET_S table, at most 0. /v1/crawl/google/play-app and /v1/crawl/google/news keep 5 s. /v1/search/bing gets 22 s, because Bing's decoys come from Bing's side and the crawler gives up on a Bing call at 20 s (auto-sns-agent 4940339b9); of 239 prod Bing calls from 11-24 to 11-26, 4.2% of the 200s answered after 20 s. It reads the answered calls' data_api_call charge rows in product.usage_events, and a route with under 20 answered calls that day reads the p90 of its newest 20 answered calls up to the day's end, because from 11-14 the routes got 1 to 11 answered calls a day and the duty read error every run. It counts internal orgs because no is_internal = 0 org called these routes from 10-20 to 11-02 and the owner's own calls come from internal orgs.

metrics.label: Customer prod 5xx share of keyed calls, last full UTC day (ClickHouse product.customer_usage_events, less org_test_)

Most seconds a slow route's p90 sits over its own target (Bing 22 s, Google Play and News 5 s), every org, last full UTC day (ClickHouse data_api_call duration_ms, a quiet day reads the route's newest 20 answered calls)

onMiss: Read the flagged customer_5xx slices: each names the operation, status, error code, request id and org. Match each 5xx to its prod crawler span with one small ops/bin/ch-ro prod query (otel.otel_traces, SpanKind='Server', ParentSpanId='', production, an hours window, SETTINGS max_threads=2 and a log_comment), as ~/work/portal-customer-failures/q-*.sql does, and read the request's handle from that span, then read it again through api.virev.ai with a throwaway key: mint it with `npx convex run apiPortal/keys:ensureDefault` and prod's admin key (CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_URL https://convex.virev.ai and CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_ADMIN_KEY from apps/ci/.env) for an org_duty_<tag>_<ms> org, credit it with apiPortal/adminLedger:grantCredit, and remove it after with apiPortal/keys:cleanupTestOrg, because prod's /api/test/seed answers 404 since cac8db349. A proof that needs PostHog firsts or a real charge uses an org_test_<tag>_<ms> id instead, because org_duty_ orgs are house orgs (convex/org/houseOrgs.json) that pay nothing and send no firsts. Group the 5xx by cause. A cause on our side (crawler verdict, portal mapping, docs or error text) gets one fix job unless one is live; it lands with a test on dev/sieun, crawler fixes reach prod through the crawler ops train and portal fixes through the release owner's promote (c154). Count a deploy hole or a host move as its own cause and name it. A source_errors miss fixes the prod ClickHouse read through Grafana (estate_ch_prod with the grafana-read key). A long stretch with no keyed call row in the day line means ledger rows went missing, so read Vercel's api-portal request logs for that stretch (vercel logs --project auto-sns-api --environment production --json). No customer email goes out without the owner's ok (c37). A slow_route_over_target_s miss: read the slow_routes line, which names each route's p90 against its own target. A route over its target gets one fix job on its slowest calls unless one is live. Bing over 22 s means the crawler's 20 s give-up (4940339b9) is not holding, so that job starts by asking Crawler guy. The line names a route's pooled newest 20 calls and their oldest time when its day was quiet, and at 999999 a route has under 20 answered calls in all of product.usage_events. All on target: end the turn with no message.
